title: Lightweight admission rubric and rollback contract for uncertified models
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: engineering and runtime teams frequently receive community-submitted open models that pass basic validation but surface subtle runtime incompatibilities (tokenization edge cases, kv cache layout differences, unexpected attention patterns) after being enabled in the catalog. This leads to production regressions or silent cost increases when unpinned variants are routed. Goal: define a compact, low-friction admission rubric and an explicit rollback/soft-pin contract for 'uncertified' (community) models that balances time-to-availability with safety, operational overhead, and deterministic rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A concise admission rubric (<=6 checks) exists and is published to the intake form; checks include runtime sanity pass, tokenization mapping verification, expected latency envelope, per-sample KV-cache memory delta within threshold, and model provenance metadata.
Onboarded uncertified models are automatically labeled 'uncertified' in the catalog UI and API with clear behavioral warnings and default soft-pin to a conservative runtime variant.

A deterministic rollback contract is documented: rollback triggers, ownership handoff, automatic traffic drain window (configurable default 5 minutes), and post-rollback telemetry collection requirements.
Console shows a single-click 'soft-pin' and 'rollback' action for the model entry that creates an audit log, opens a runbook link, and pings the on-call channel.

E2E test harness includes one regression test that runs the admission rubric against a small benchmark set and a simulated KV/latency stress scenario; it must pass in staging before catalog entry becomes searchable.
SRE and Runtime teams approve the rubric and rollback contract in writing (email or PR comment) before the change is promoted to prod catalog.
Metrics: number of post-onboard incidents attributable to uncatalogued runtime incompatibilities decreases by 50% over the next quarter (tracked via incident tags).
scope_changes: Start with a lightweight rubric for new community models only (do not apply to curated/verified models). Excludes automated ML-quality evals and user-facing cost-estimates in phase 1. Phase 2 may add stricter semantic checks and automated model tuning guidance.
plan: 1) Finalize rubric draft with Runtime & SRE (2 weeks). 2) Implement intake form flags + auto-labeling + UI banner (3 weeks). 3) Add one-click soft-pin/rollback with audit log and default traffic-drain behavior (2 weeks). 4) Wire staging E2E test and runbook links (1 week). 5) Pilot with 10 community models, gather telemetry, iterate (4 weeks).
risks:
- False negatives: rubric may approve models that later fail under heavy load.
- False positives: overly strict checks may block valuable models and increase onboarding friction.
- Operational burden: SRE may see more alerts during pilot until rollback behavior is tuned.
- User communication: customers must clearly understand what 'uncertified' means to avoid trust erosion.
open_questions: What constitutes an acceptable KV-cache memory delta for different model families (Llama-family vs transformer-big)?
Should the default soft-pin variant be region-specific (to account for hardware differences)?
Who signs off on emergency rollbacks outside office hours (on-call rotation or PM-owned)?
Do we expose a catalog API flag that allows partners to opt out of soft-pin behavior?
notes_and_decisions:
2025-02-18: Agreed to keep rubric <=6 checks to limit friction.
2025-02-25: Default traffic drain window set to 5 minutes, configurable per-entry.
2025-02-28: Decided to require SRE sign-off in PR comments before searchability.
implementation_notes: Engineering to instrument per-model telemetry tags (latency_95, kv_mem_delta, tokenization_mismatch_rate). UI will reuse existing ‘model flags’ component. Add audit log entry when soft-pin/rollback actions are taken. Runbook template in Confluence to be copied for each model entry.
communication_plan: Announce pilot in #product-announcements and #sre-weekly. Provide a one-page intake rubric summary to community contributors and include a checkbox in the intake form acknowledging soft-pin policy.
post_launch_actions: Collect pilot telemetry for 6 weeks, convene a retro with SRE/Runtime/Legal, iterate rubric checks and thresholds, and produce a PRD for phase 2 enhancements.
customer-facing_message: New community models will be labeled 'uncertified' and may be served from conservative runtime variants. We will proactively soft-pin or roll back models that cause runtime regressions. Contact support for expedited review.
